About.metaTitle: About Neev — built for civil-services aspirants, honest about where you stand
About.leadTitle: Built on the belief that strong foundations create stronger futures.
About.leadSubtitle: Neev scores your Mains answers like an examiner and gives you a fact-checked study chapter for every topic in the syllabus. A bilingual prep app for civil-services aspirants — Prelims, Mains and CSAT. Hindi and English are equal here, and we're honest about where you stand, not padded with encouragement.
About.stat1Label: fact-checked study chapters — one for every topic in the syllabus
About.stat2Label: verified past-year questions, every paper from 2016 to 2026
About.stat3Label: rubric dimensions every Mains answer is scored on
About.accuracyIntro: Most of what makes prep material wrong is unverified answers and copied facts. Here's the part most apps skip.
About.accuracy1Title: Official answer keys, not coaching guesses
About.accuracy1Body: Prelims MCQ answers are cross-checked against the official commission answer keys wherever one exists. Where only a coaching reproduction is available, we say so instead of passing it off as official.
About.accuracy2Title: A blind second opinion on every question
About.accuracy2Body: An independent AI solves each question blind, without seeing the key. Any answer that disagrees is flagged for a human — never trusted silently.
About.accuracy3Title: A human review gate before anything publishes
About.accuracy3Body: Disputed questions go to a review queue instead of going live automatically. Every study chapter's decisive facts are checked against a real source, and a chapter can't publish while a single claim stays unresolved.
About.accuracy4Body: "Report this question" sits on every question you see. Flag a wrong answer or explanation and it lands in that same review queue.
About.flagshipBody1: Write a Mains answer — typed, or a photo of your handwritten pages — and get it scored against a six-dimension rubric modeled on how examiners for your exam actually grade: structure & flow, content coverage, keywords & concepts, examples & data, presentation, and word limit. Each dimension gets a score and a written reason, not just a number.
About.flagshipBody2: It's grounded, not guessing. Before scoring, it retrieves the syllabus content, past-year questions, and study-chapter material for your exact question and evaluates against that — then shows you a model answer and the points you missed.
About.flagshipBody3: And it's honest. An empty, off-topic, or copy-pasted answer is scored as exactly that. The goal is an accurate read of where you stand, not encouragement for its own sake.
About.seriesTitle: The second flagship: a scheduled test series
About.seriesBody1: Most of what makes an institute's test series work is not the questions — it is the calendar. You know months ahead which paper falls on which date, what it covers and what to read before it. Neev publishes the same thing: every paper with its date, its topics and its sources, for Prelims and Mains, on both exams we support.
About.seriesBody2: The rules are the market's own, implemented exactly. A paper stays locked until its date, for everyone — that is the only thing that makes a shared rank worth reading. It opens on the date and never closes, so falling a week behind costs you the rank on that paper and nothing else. Sit it inside the ranked window and your result carries your position and the size of the cohort it was measured against; sit it later and the score, the per-question review and the topic analysis are identical, minus the rank.
About.seriesBody3: Each paper is assembled shortly before it opens, so it draws on the newest approved questions in the bank, and full-length papers follow the commission's own notified pattern for question count, duration and negative marking. The series sits in Max, the top of our three plans — everything above stays where it was.
About.pillarsSub: One honest sentence each — no overclaiming.
About.pillar1Body: A full, fact-audited chapter for every syllabus topic — not a quick summary — that doubles as the grounding the mentor and evaluator read from.
About.pillar2Body: A fresh quiz each day, mixing your weak topics, spaced-repetition PYQs, and this week's current affairs — never just a random slice.
About.pillar3Body: Ask a doubt and get an answer grounded in the same chapters and PYQs you study from, with the exact source cited.
About.pillar4Body: Daily summaries written in our own words, with a regional lens where your exam has one, and links back to the syllabus topics they touch.
About.pillar5Body: Share an answer for peer review or ask in a discussion thread — every post is screened before others see it.
About.pillar6Body: Honest progress tracking — mastery decays if you stop practicing a topic, and mock scores compare you against real cut-offs.
About.ctaSub: Free to start — no card needed.
About.supportBody: For a wrong answer or explanation on a specific question, use "Report this question" right on that question — it goes straight to our review queue. For anything else — your account, billing, or a bug — email us.

Faq.title: Frequently asked questions
Faq.subtitle: Real questions, straight answers.
Faq.a1: Mostly. Practice PYQs, the daily quiz, current affairs and spaced-repetition revision are free and uncapped, and every new account starts with a 7-day Pro trial — no card needed. After the trial, Free keeps all of that plus the top 5 study chapters per paper, 10 mentor messages a day, and 3 AI answer evaluations in total (not per month — we'd rather say so than have you find out). Pro lifts evaluations to 60 a month and adds handwritten-answer OCR, full mock tests, micro-drills, every study chapter, and the magazine PDF.
Faq.q2: How accurate is the AI evaluation?
Faq.a2: It's grounded, not guessing — the model retrieves the syllabus content and past-year questions relevant to your specific answer before scoring it, against a six-dimension rubric modeled on your exam's own Mains marking. It's calibrated against sample strong, average, and off-topic answers to keep ranking and scoring consistent — but it's an AI evaluator, not a substitute for a real examiner. Treat the score and feedback as a fast, informed second opinion, not a guaranteed final mark.
Faq.a3: Yes — Hindi is first-class here, not a fallback. The interface, study chapters, mentor answers, and evaluation feedback are all fully bilingual, with real Devanagari typography. One honest caveat: some older past-year-question Hindi text is machine-translated from the original exam PDFs, since their Hindi text layer doesn't extract cleanly — we're steadily replacing it with the real printed Hindi.
Faq.a4: Each exam we cover is mapped to its OWN syllabus and exam pattern — Prelims, Mains and CSAT — rather than one generic civil-services template stretched to fit, which is why adding an exam takes a full syllabus and question-bank ingest rather than a switch. You pick yours during onboarding and can change it later in your profile.
Faq.a5: Your answers, attempts, and progress are used to power your own prep — scoring, spaced-repetition scheduling, mastery tracking, and analytics. Your account data is scoped to you at the database level (row-level security), and answer evaluation runs through Anthropic's Claude API. We don't sell your data.
Faq.q6: How do I report a wrong answer or explanation?
Faq.a6: Use the flag icon — "Report this question" — on the question itself, wherever you see it (practice, revision, PYQ lists). That routes straight into our review queue, the same one every question passes before publishing. For anything that isn't about a specific question — your account, billing, or a bug — use the contact page instead, so it lands in the right place.
Faq.a7: Yes. Payments run through Razorpay (UPI, cards, netbanking, wallets) — Neev never sees or stores your card, UPI, or bank details; they go directly to Razorpay's PCI-compliant systems, the same ones used across most Indian apps taking UPI payments.

Privacy.title: Privacy Policy
Privacy.subtitle: What personal data we collect, why, and your rights under India's DPDP Act.
Privacy.intro: Neev (नींव) ("Neev", "we", "us") is a service operated by Neev Study, a sole proprietorship, at neevstudy.com. This Privacy Policy explains what personal data we collect, why, who we share it with, and your rights. We act as a Data Fiduciary under India's Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 ("DPDP Act"). By using the Service you consent to the processing described here for the stated purposes.
Privacy.s1Body:
- **Account and authentication data.** Your email address (and, if you sign in with Google where available, your Google account identifier and name). Authentication is handled by our provider, Supabase Auth. Your password, if you set one, is stored by Supabase in hashed form; we never see it in plain text.
- **Profile data.** Display name, preferred language (Hindi/English), target exam year, medium, study-hours preference, and a public community handle if you use community features.
- **Your submissions.** Descriptive answers you type; photos of handwritten answers you upload; the text extracted from those photos (OCR); custom questions or prompts you enter; and questions you ask the AI mentor.
- **Learning activity.** Your MCQ attempts and answers, quiz and mock-test results and timings, spaced-repetition cards and reviews, saved notes, study plans, and reading and progress signals.
- **Community data.** Discussion posts, votes, answers you choose to share for peer review, and reports you file. These are visible to other users under your handle or display name.
- **Usage analytics.** First-party product events (for example, that a chapter was opened) tied to your account, used to operate and improve the Service. We do NOT use third-party advertising or tracking analytics (no Google Analytics, Meta, Mixpanel, and the like).
- **Device and notification data.** If you enable push notifications, your browser's push subscription (endpoint and keys) and browser or device string.
- **Payment data.** When you buy Pro, our payment partner Razorpay processes your payment. We receive and store order and payment identifiers, amount, currency, and subscription status — never your full card number or CVV (see 'Payments — Razorpay' below).
- **Trial-integrity signal.** On sign-up we store a one-way salted hash of your IP address (never the raw IP) solely to detect abuse of the free-trial system. It is reviewed only manually and is never used to profile you.

Email addresses and any phone number are held within our authentication provider (Supabase Auth), not in our application profile records.
Privacy.s2Body: We use your data to provide and operate the Service; to run AI evaluations, OCR, and the mentor and generate your feedback, scores and model answers; to track your progress and personalise study recommendations; to process payments and manage your plan; to send account and service-related communications; to keep the Service secure and prevent abuse; to comply with law; and to improve the Service using aggregated or first-party usage data.
Privacy.s3Title: AI processing and the data we send to AI providers
Privacy.s3Body:
Several features are powered by third-party AI providers. When you use these features, the relevant content is transmitted to the provider to generate a result:

- **Anthropic** (Claude models) receives: your typed answer text and question when you request an evaluation; your uploaded handwritten page images for transcription (OCR) and, for the presentation score, the first page image; your mentor and doubt questions and conversation; and, where you use in-depth mentor research, your topic (which may be used with the provider's web-search tool). Community posts are also screened for abuse, spam, and personal information by an AI model.
- **OpenAI** receives text (for example, your mentor question and question text) to create numeric "embeddings" used for search and to find relevant study material. Your descriptive answer text is not sent to OpenAI.

These providers process the content to return a result to us. Under their commercial API terms as of the date of this Policy, Anthropic and OpenAI state that they do not use API inputs or outputs to train their models, and delete them within their standard retention window (generally up to 30 days for abuse-monitoring). We do not control these providers; please refer to their own policies for details. We send only what a feature needs to function.
Privacy.s4Body: Payments are processed by Razorpay Software Private Limited. Your card, UPI, or bank details are entered on Razorpay's secure checkout and are handled by Razorpay under its own privacy policy and PCI-DSS obligations. **We do not receive or store your full card number or CVV.** We store the payment and order identifiers, amount, subscription status, and the payment processor's transaction records needed to provide your subscription and meet legal and accounting obligations.
Privacy.s5Body: Account emails — such as login one-time-passwords, sign-up confirmation, and password reset — are sent through our authentication provider, Supabase Auth, using its built-in email service. We do not currently run separate marketing email campaigns.
Privacy.s6Body:
We do not sell your personal data. We share it only with service providers that help us run the Service, under their terms:

- **Supabase** — hosting, database, storage, and authentication. Involves your account, profile, all your learning data, and uploaded images.
- **Anthropic** — AI evaluation, OCR, mentor, and content moderation. Involves your answer text, uploaded images, mentor questions, and community post text.
- **OpenAI** — text embeddings for search and study-material matching. Involves your mentor questions and question text.
- **Razorpay** — payment processing. Involves payment and transaction data (no full card data is held by us).

If we enable error-monitoring (Sentry) in production, limited diagnostic and request data may be shared with it; this Policy will reflect it when active. We may also disclose data where required by law or to protect rights and safety.
Privacy.s7Body: Some providers above (notably the AI providers) process data on servers outside India. Where we transfer personal data internationally, we do so in accordance with the DPDP Act and applicable law. By using the AI features you consent to this transfer for the purpose of providing them.
Privacy.s8Body: We retain your personal data for as long as your account is active and as needed to provide the Service, and thereafter as required to comply with legal, tax, and accounting obligations or to resolve disputes. Uploaded handwritten images and their transcriptions are retained to show your submission history unless you request deletion. AI providers retain API data only for their own limited retention window (see 'AI processing' above).
Privacy.s9Body:
Under the DPDP Act you have the right to:

- **Access** your data — you can download your practice attempts and answer submissions with their AI evaluations from Profile → Settings → Export my data. For a copy of other data we hold, contact us.
- **Correct or update** your profile data in the app, or by contacting us.
- **Erase your data or delete your account** — self-service account deletion is not yet available in the app; to request deletion, email support@neevstudy.com and we will delete your account and associated personal data, subject to any records we must retain by law.
- **Withdraw consent** for optional processing (for example, disable push notifications in Settings), and **nominate** another person to exercise your rights in the event of death or incapacity, as provided by the DPDP Act.
- **Grievance redressal** — see 'Grievance and contact' below.
Privacy.s10Body: We protect your data with measures including: strict per-user database access controls (row-level security), so one user cannot read another user's data; authenticated, token-verified API access; private storage for your uploaded images, isolated to your own account so no other user can access them; signed, verified payment webhooks; a salted hash instead of a raw IP for the trial signal; and encryption in transit (HTTPS/TLS) for data moving between you, us, and our providers. Data at rest is protected by our hosting provider's encryption. No method of transmission or storage is completely secure, and we cannot guarantee absolute security.
Privacy.s11Body: The Service is intended for candidates preparing for the UPPSC examinations and is not directed at children. We do not knowingly collect personal data from children. If you believe a child has provided us personal data, contact us and we will delete it.
Privacy.s12Body: For any questions, requests, or grievances about your personal data or this Policy, contact our grievance contact at support@neevstudy.com. We will acknowledge and address grievances within the timelines required by the DPDP Act (within 90 days).
Privacy.s13Body: We may update this Policy. Material changes will be reflected in the "Last updated" date and, where appropriate, notified in the app. Continued use after changes means you accept the updated Policy.

revision.highlight1Body: Neev runs on FSRS, the same family of spaced-repetition algorithm used by Anki — it adapts to how well you actually know each card instead of showing everything every 3 days regardless.

revision.faqQ1: What is FSRS, and how is it different from a regular flashcard system?

gamifiedPractice.faqA4: No — it's you against your own past attempt on the same test, question by question. There's no public leaderboard here; it's a private way to see if you're genuinely getting faster and more accurate over time.

uppsc.introTitle: What the UPPSC PCS exam is
uppsc.introBody1: The Uttar Pradesh Public Service Commission runs the Provincial Civil Services examination — commonly written UPPSC PCS, UP PCS or UPPCS — in three stages: a Preliminary paper set that screens, a descriptive Main examination that decides merit, and an interview. Only the Main examination and the interview carry marks into the final merit list; Prelims marks do not. That is why the Preliminary examination is best treated as a threshold to clear rather than a score to maximise.
uppsc.introBody2: The Main examination was restructured for 2023: the optional subject was abolished and two compulsory General Studies papers focused on Uttar Pradesh were added in its place. That is the largest change to this exam in a decade, and it means preparation built on pre-2023 advice is preparation for an exam that no longer exists. The pattern below is read from the commission's current notification rather than restated from memory.

upsc.introTitle: What the UPSC Civil Services examination is
upsc.introBody1: The Civil Services Examination — the UPSC CSE, the exam that recruits to the IAS, IPS and IFS — runs in three stages: a Preliminary screening test, a descriptive Main examination, and a Personality Test. Two of the Main examination papers are language qualifying papers, and unlike an ordinary qualifying paper, failing one means your other papers are never evaluated at all.
upsc.introBody2: The Main examination also carries two papers in a candidate-chosen optional subject. Neev does not cover the optionals: there are around twenty-five of them, two papers each, and we hold no data for any — so the syllabus tree here deliberately excludes them rather than pretending otherwise. Everything below covers the compulsory papers.
